audit_scope: independent recomputation from the 20 raw cell artifacts and frozen Stage B rules
verdict: numeric and protocol result reproduced exactly

scoped_result.interpretation: service/SLO completion-window knee, not a hard-error or absolute throughput ceiling
scoped_result.runtime_scope: unchanged W1/RT1, 64-token unique-miss, direct Pod IP, one HTTP/2 connection, 180 seconds

reporting_correction.issue: the bundled Stage A preregistration does not document a five-to-ten-block extension rule; the extension protocol was frozen after Stage A and before Stage B
reporting_correction.recommended_language: Across five original blocks and a five-block extension whose protocol and analysis were frozen before extension load, the combined 10-block rule confirmed the scoped knee.

caveats: At 42 RPS all requests eventually returned OK; more than 1% completed after the plateau and conditional successful-within-window p99 rose to seconds.
One Stage A 42-RPS cell had a liveness timeout 40 seconds before plateau; it caused no restart and no plateau or post-plateau health event.
All topology reports warned that node housekeeping CPUs split SMT; the measured target cpuset 5,149 was unaffected.
Driver pod runtime imageID and node were not persisted per cell; pinned configuration, driver self-report, archived build evidence, and target identity are present.
Model and tokenizer hashes were supplied identities and were not rehashed from the PVC in every cell.
The result does not cover ClusterIP routing, same-Pod recovery, default W4 behavior, or 20-50 replica scale-out.
